wm_goal_570.semantics: 10 future reference frames, each concatenates 24 joint positions then 24 joint velocities; frames at t,t+5,...,t+45 clipped independently at each reference last frame.
10 reference ROOT positions expressed relative to current robot root (root-body XYZ), 3 per frame.
10 reference ROOT orientations expressed relative to current root, rotation6d, 6 per frame.

critical_facts: Deleted30 are relative reference ROOT translations, not TCP positions, not 30 arbitrary privileged channels.
make_motion_task always returns compute_wm_goal second item. Switching actor_obs from proprio to rep_state does not add these30 back.

Goal has no independent event phase, no explicit pregrasp frozen endpoint, no measured door angle or TCP-handle relative displacement. Reference joint/root-orientation sequence supplies intended movement implicitly.
At 20ms control and stride5 the 10-frame goal window spans current through +0.9s. Actor observes advancing reference clock, not independently stalled event stage.

proven_input_invariance_and_its_limits.status: Analytical consequence of directly inspected source; not a new numerical physical experiment or frozen-weight inference run.
proven_input_invariance_and_its_limits.translation: For a fixed reference frame, preserve all10 history joint/velocity/angular/gravity/action fields and current root orientation, but translate root XYZ of each history sample by a common delta. Current77×10 proprio and540goal are unchanged: proprio ignores root position, goal retains relative orientations but drops relative positions. Any fixed Actor/normalizers therefore returns exactly the same command for those identical inputs.
proven_input_invariance_and_its_limits.linear_velocity: Changing only root body linear velocity while holding angular/joint/history sensor fields fixed is also invisible to the current proprio sensor. Robot58 would distinguish it; robot58 height distinguishes vertical position but neither cures XY aliasing.
proven_input_invariance_and_its_limits.critic_difference: WM representation75 and Critic input75+570+5 include object geometry and relative reference translations. They can distinguish states that Actor aliases. Better WM state prediction and differentiated per-state gradients cannot alone grant Actor missing information; conflicting control requirements can be averaged at a common Actor input. The presence and size of such actual conflicts remains to be measured.
proven_input_invariance_and_its_limits.ground_symmetry: scripts/p6_scene.py uses one plane and fixed passive door. Before door contact, translating an otherwise identical robot trajectory over a homogeneous floor preserves proprio dynamics in ideal exact arithmetic. This supports a structural absolute-position observability concern, but current real solver trajectories and actual required success rates still need measured checks.

C_case_evidence.facts: C02/C03 set initial dx=+/-0.05m; C04/C05 dy=+/-0.05m. Initial joint/home/previous-action history and reference remain fixed; only rootXY changes in these four cases. No reference alignment occurs.

root_review_of_original_reward.body_target_reanchoring: Target root XY is reanchored to predicted root XY; target root Z retained; body targets rotated by predicted-to-target root yaw difference.
root_review_of_original_reward.interpretation: The 0.3m Gaussian kernel is not an error tolerance. The 100:1 length-scale comparison is not evidence of a bug or permission to change the reward. Root absolute tracking remains a separate positive term.
root_review_of_original_reward.unresolved: Derivative correctness, actual return-gradient direction and the contribution of these terms on the critical pregrasp states have not been physically tested in this review.
